identity.gender_note: A masculine given name; also used as a surname.

core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ahmad (Arabic أحمد, ʾAḥmad) is an Arabic male name from the root ḥ-m-d, “to praise”. It means “most praised” or “most praiseworthy” and is one of the best-known names of the Prophet Muhammad, which is why it is common across the Muslim world.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Ahmad comes from the verb ḥamida, “to thank, to praise”. It shares its root with Muhammad, Mahmud, Hamid and Hamad. In the Qur'an (61:6) Isa (Jesus) foretells a messenger named Ahmad, which most Muslim scholars understand as Muhammad.

etymology.morphology: Elative (afʿal) form of the root ḥ-m-d.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From the root ح م د (ḥ-m-d), verb ḥamida “to thank or to praise”.

origin.origin_explanation: Arabic, spread with Islam. Its transliteration has one of the largest numbers of spelling variants of any name (Ahmed, Ahmet, Akhmad, Achmad…).

religion.primary_association: Islamic — a name of the Prophet Muhammad
religion.religious_explanation: In Surah al-Saff (61:6) Isa (Jesus) announces a messenger to come “whose name is Ahmad”; most Muslim scholars take this to mean Muhammad. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari report Muhammad naming himself Ahmad. Some Western scholars, such as W. Montgomery Watt, argued that Ahmad was not used as a proper name for Muhammad until the second Islamic century.

quranic_status.note: Prophecy attributed to Isa of a messenger named Ahmad.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: Some traditions regard Ahmad as the Prophet's more esoteric name; some Muslim scholars also compared it with the biblical “Paraclete”, a view that is not universal.

urdu.meaning: سب سے زیادہ تعریف کیا گیا

pronunciation.note: Egyptian Arabic and Turkish say Ah-med / Ah-met.

name_variants.variant_notes: Ahmed (Egypt, English), Ahmet (Turkish), Achmad (Indonesian), Akhmad (Central Asian/Russian transliteration).

known_linguistic_history: Ahmad is linked to the Qur'anic prophecy in 61:6.
Used as a personal name throughout Islamic history, e.g. Ahmad ibn Hanbal (founder of the Hanbali school).
historical_context.historical_person_association: The Prophet Muhammad, called Ahmad in Qur'an 61:6.

modern_usage.modern_context: Common throughout the Muslim world; Ahmed is the usual Egyptian/English spelling and Ahmet the Turkish one.

faq.a: “Most praised” or “most praiseworthy”, from the Arabic root ḥ-m-d, “to praise”.

faq.q: Is Ahmad mentioned in the Qur'an?
faq.a: Yes. In Qur'an 61:6 Isa (Jesus) foretells a messenger “whose name is Ahmad”, understood by most Muslim scholars as Muhammad.

faq.q: Is Ahmad the same as Muhammad?
faq.a: They are different names from the same root, ḥ-m-d. Ahmad is considered one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad.

faq.q: Ahmad or Ahmed — which is correct?
faq.a: Both. They transliterate the same Arabic أحمد; Ahmed reflects Egyptian and Turkish pronunciation.
Muhammad, Mahmud, Hamid and Hamad all come from ḥ-m-d.

islamic_naming_context.context: Given in honour of the Prophet, often as the first element of compound names (Ahmad Ali, Ahmad Raza).
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Chosen for its link with the Prophet and its meaning “most praised”.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: The meaning comes from Arabic grammar; its religious weight comes from the Qur'anic verse and the Prophet.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ahmad total 9, associated with compassion, idealism and completion. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.
